checklist.content: The comparison panel supports anchor point linkage: clicking on the difference will jump to the corresponding location in the document, while the difference will be highlighted in the original document area.
checklist.bug: The comparison page cannot jump to the corresponding location in the original document; there are no anchor links.

checklist.content: Scene comparison only supports a maximum of 2 scenes to be compared simultaneously.
The global search only retrieves content visible in the current scene; hidden content outside the current scene is not included in the search, thus avoiding interference from irrelevant results.
Provide real-time visual feedback when users use the search function.
Different differences are highlighted in different colors in the comparison function.
The content of a webpage should be appropriate for the specific context of the webpage.
The content in different steps must correspond to the content of that step.
The comparison page allows users to view the full details of the differences, preventing any questions from the user.
checklist.bug: When the text is too long, the incomplete content is displayed directly, and there is no direct jump, forcing users to view it manually.

instruction: I want a webpage that allows me to search various job listings. This webpage should allow me to filter results by job type (full-time, part-time, contract) and location (city name). After applying the filters and performing a search, I should be able to save this set of filters and name them, such as "Remote Technology Jobs" or "New York City Marketing Jobs." Later, I should be able to view the saved search list, clicking on any of them to immediately reapply the filters and see the updated results. New features: 1. Job comparison function, supporting the selection of multiple jobs for generating a comparison table, intuitively displaying differences in core dimensions such as salary, location, and experience requirements; 2. Search history management function, automatically recording recent search records, supporting individual deletion and one-click clearing, and allowing quick re-search by clicking on a history record.

checklist.content: Users can filter search results in real time by job type (full-time, part-time, contract) and location (city name).
Users can save the current combination of filter criteria and enter a custom name for it (such as "Remote Technical Positions").
Users can view and click on any item in the "Saved Searches" list, and the system must immediately reapply the corresponding filtering rules.
checklist.bug: Saved history cannot be searched again, and the system cannot filter the corresponding rules.

checklist.content: Users can select multiple job cards and click the comparison button to generate a horizontal comparison table that includes salary, location, and experience requirements.
The system must automatically record users' search terms and filtering operations in the "Search History".
Users can click on a single record in the search history to quickly trigger a search, or perform single-record deletion or one-click clearing of the history.
Users can search by job, company, or keyword.
checklist.bug: Users cannot search by job, company, or keyword.

checklist.content: If a user attempts to save a filter using an existing name, the system should prompt that the filter is duplicated or ask whether to overwrite it.
checklist.bug: It can save duplicate names without prompting a message.

checklist.content: When reapplying a saved search, the system must ensure that the search results are accurate.
The "Generate Comparison" button should be disabled when no positions are selected or only one position is selected.
When a user adds a job to the comparison list, the page should provide clear visual feedback (such as a small dot count or a change in the floating window).
Before clicking "Clear Search History with One Click," the system should prompt for secondary confirmation to prevent users from accidentally clicking and losing their records.
Saving filter criteria should be done via a modal or overlay, with an immediate visual notification of "successful save" upon submission.
When the mouse hovers over a saved search term, the specific filter details of the query should be displayed for the user to confirm.
Key metrics (salary, experience, location) in job comparison tables must be highlighted so that users can easily identify the differences.
checklist.bug: Partial highlighting

checklist.content: The saved search list should clearly display the user-defined name and the specific filter parameters included in the search.
Search history should accurately display search keywords, and if only filters were applied, filter tags should be displayed.
After filtering the job list, the system must accurately display the total number of current search results.

instruction: I want a web page where users can describe a problem they're facing by filling out a simple form with fields like problem category (technical, business, personal, academic), problem description, and urgency level. After submitting, the page displays a list of suggested solution approaches with brief explanations for each. Users should be able to view all their previously submitted problems and the solutions that were generated for them.Users can mark whether a solution is available. The system will calculate dynamic weights and rank the solutions in real time based on multiple factors such as availability, matching degree with the current problem, operational complexity, and adaptability to urgency. Users can also customize the weight ratio of each factor.

checklist.content: Users can fill out a form to describe the problem.
The form can be configured with fields such as issue category, issue description, and urgency level.
A corresponding solution is generated after the user submits it.
Users can view the details of each solution.
Each solution includes basic information such as name, brief description, operational complexity (low/medium/high), and urgency level (low/medium/high/urgent).
Each plan is equipped with a two-way "Available / Unavailable" indicator button.
checklist.bug: There are only available tags, no unavailable tags, and the situation where users cannot tag an answer because they haven't seen it is not considered.

checklist.content: Users can view detailed information about example problem records.
The system calculates weights and ranks solutions in real time based on four core factors: solution availability, matching degree, operational complexity, and urgency suitability.
The system provides a weight configuration panel, allowing users to manually adjust the weight ratio of each factor.
The system automatically calculates the availability of each answer.
The system automatically calculates the degree to which the answer matches the question.
The system automatically calculates the complexity of the answer.
The system automatically calculates the urgency of the answer to the question.
The system displays the final weighted total score.
When a user modifies the weighting percentages, the scores for each question are updated in real time.
Record the different weights for different questions, ensuring that the weighting of each question's answer dimension is independent of the others.
checklist.bug: Only the same weight percentage can be saved.

checklist.content: The sum of all weighted percentages must be 100%; a warning will be given if it exceeds or falls short.
checklist.bug: Calculations will still be performed even if the amount exceeds or falls short.

checklist.content: The form cannot be submitted without filling in the required information.
The form description of the problem has a character limit, and visual feedback is given when the character limit is exceeded or exceeded.
Provide visual feedback when users mark an available/unavailable status.
Real-time feedback on score changes when users modify weighting percentages.
The proposed solution needs to match the content and type of the problem.
checklist.bug: The solutions given for different problems are the same.

checklist.content: The scores given for each dimension should match the degree of fit between the answer and the question.
checklist.bug: Mismatch

instruction: I want a webpage where users can search for historical decisions and their outcomes. They can enter keywords to find decisions, view matching result lists with names and outcome summaries, and click to check full details including the conditions and final results. The search function supports queries by decision name, outcome and conditions, as well as multi-dimensional filtering, search history recording, decision bookmarking and management, and batch import/export in Excel/CSV/PDF formats.

checklist.content: Users can enter search terms to find decisions. The search function supports searching by decision name, result summary, and decision criteria, and returns a list of matching decisions.

Users can use multi-dimensional filters (such as by time range, decision type, result type, relevant responsible persons, etc.) to combine and filter the decision list, and the filtering results are accurate.
The system records the user's search history, allowing the user to easily view and quickly reuse previous search keywords or filter combinations.
Users can add important decisions to their personal favorites and can categorize or remove saved decisions.
Users can batch export multiple decisions in Excel format. The exported file contains complete fields such as decision name, result, and conditions, and is correctly formatted.
checklist.bug: Multiple selections not allowed, only all can be selected.

checklist.content: Users can export multiple decisions in batches in CSV format. The exported files contain complete data and conform to the CSV standard format.
checklist.bug: Multiple selections not allowed, only all can be selected.

checklist.content: Users can export one or more decision details in PDF format. The PDF file is complete, clearly formatted, and includes necessary metadata (such as the export time).
checklist.bug: Multiple selections not allowed, only all can be selected.

checklist.content: Users can import decision records in batches by uploading Excel files, and the system can correctly parse the file content and create corresponding decision entries.
Users can import decision records in batches by uploading CSV files; the system can handle standard CSV format and import data correctly.
In the decision list or details page, users can edit or delete individual decisions, and the edited data will be synchronously updated to all related views.
The user's decision to add a item to their favorites is clearly visually indicated in both the search results list and the details page (e.g., a highlighted favorites icon).
When a user clears their search history or removes a favorite item, the system will require secondary confirmation to prevent accidental operations.
checklist.bug: No secondary confirmation required

checklist.content: After a user performs a critical operation (such as deletion or batch import) on any page, the page status should be updated promptly and accurately to reflect the latest data.
If the file format is incorrect or required fields are missing during the import process, the system will provide a clear error message and prevent the import.
checklist.bug: The absence will not prevent

checklist.content: The system can handle concurrent operations correctly, such as searching or filtering while importing in batches, without causing data corruption or page crashes.
The search results list clearly displays the name and result summary of each decision, and users can access the full details page by clicking on the list item.
The decision details page fully displays the decision name, a summary of the results, the specific conditions that led to the decision, and a detailed description of the final result.
All batch import/export operations have clear progress indicators and provide a success or failure notification upon completion.

instruction: I want to create a webpage that implements a purely front-end-based job competency modeling and simulation system. HR professionals can search for competency models by job name or keywords, and the page will display a list of results and access detailed information. On the details page, the system needs to represent the competency model as a directed weighted graph structure, with nodes representing competencies and edges representing dependencies or reinforcement relationships. Users can directly drag and drop to adjust competency levels, modify weights, or temporarily enable/disable certain competencies. The page needs to recalculate competency coverage, critical paths, and risk competency gaps in real time after each structural change, and immediately alert users to potential problems. The system should provide a general job competency model template library, allowing HR professionals to quickly build models and save custom templates. It should also support scenario-based simulations for recruitment, training, and promotion, simulating the impact of model adjustments under different scenarios.

checklist.content: Human resources professionals can search for competency models by job title or keywords, and the system can accurately return a list of matching models.
Users can click on any model in the search results to enter the model's details page.
Users can directly adjust the hierarchy of capabilities by dragging and dropping nodes on the front end, and the model structure remains correct after layout changes.
Users can modify the weight value of any edge, and the graph will be refreshed immediately after the modification, visually reflecting the weight change.

Users can temporarily enable or disable certain capability nodes in the graph. When disabled, the node and its related edges will be visually grayed out or hidden, and will no longer participate in subsequent calculations.
checklist.bug: This function is not available.

checklist.content: The system provides a "General Job Competency Model Template Library," which users can browse and preview by job type.
Users can retrieve any template from the template library, which will be loaded as a new model into the editing interface.
Users can save the edited model as a custom template, name it, and add a description. After saving, they can retrieve it from "My Templates" at any time.
checklist.bug: My model does not exist

checklist.content: The system supports scenario-based simulation modes such as "recruitment," "training," and "promotion," and users can switch between different scenarios.
In simulation mode, users can adjust the model structure, and the system can simulate and demonstrate the quantitative or qualitative impact of this adjustment on key indicators in the scenario.
When a user leaves the page and returns, the system should be able to restore the previously edited model state, or provide an explicit save/load mechanism.
The system can prevent invalid operations that may lead to calculation errors, such as adding dependency edges to disabled capabilities.
Each time the graph structure is modified, the system can recalculate and display the updated "capability coverage" percentage in real time.
All graph structure editing operations are smooth and responsive, with no noticeable lag or delay when the model complexity is moderate.

On the details page, the system presents the competency model in a clear, interactive, directed weighted graph structure, where nodes represent competencies and edges represent dependencies or reinforcement relationships.
After each structural change, the system can recalculate and highlight the "critical path" in the model in real time.
After each structural change, the system can analyze in real time and provide a "risk capability gap" warning.
When a potential problem is detected, the system can immediately provide a clear text or icon prompt in a prominent position on the interface.
checklist.bug: No prompt found

instruction: I want a course catalog website that implements a pure front-end course relationship analysis and enrollment simulation system. The page displays a list of courses, each including its name, credits, remaining available seats, and class schedule. The page maintains a virtual timetable for the current user; when the user enrolls in or drops a course from the course detail page, the timetable updates in real time and synchronizes changes to the remaining seat count. When opening any course, the page shows detailed information along with its complete prerequisite and dependency chains, dynamically visualized as a graph. The system must perform real-time front-end detection and warnings for multiple potential issues, including unmet prerequisites, cyclic prerequisite dependencies, time conflicts with courses already in the timetable, and enrollment risks caused by remaining seat changes. All course states, conflict warnings, dependency analysis, and timetable updates must be calculated and synchronized entirely on the front end.

checklist.content: Users can view a complete list of courses on the course catalog page. Each course in the list correctly displays its name, credits, remaining available slots, and class time.
Users can view the details page of any course, which displays complete course information (including name, credits, remaining available slots, class time, detailed description, etc.).

Users can select a course on the course details page. After selection, the number of available students for that course immediately decreases by 1, and the course is added to the user's virtual timetable.
checklist.bug: The number of available participants does not automatically decrease by one.

checklist.content: Users can "drop" a selected course on the course details page. After dropping a course, the number of remaining available students for that course immediately increases by 1, and the course is removed from the user's virtual timetable.
checklist.bug: Not automatically incremented by one

checklist.content: The user's virtual timetable will be updated in real time, accurately reflecting all currently selected courses, their class times, credits, and other information.
Users can search for courses in the course list or details page, and the search results will accurately match keywords in the course name or description.
Users can narrow down the course list display by filtering criteria such as credit range, class time, and remaining available students.
If a user withdraws from a course, and the course was previously blocked due to unmet prerequisites but now meets those prerequisites, the system should allow the user to select that course.

When a user attempts to select a course for which the prerequisites are not met, the system will clearly display the specific missing prerequisites and prevent the course selection process from proceeding.

When a user attempts to select a course that conflicts with a course in the current virtual timetable, the system will clearly display the specific course and time of the conflict and prevent the course selection operation from proceeding.
When there are 0 remaining available students for a course, the "Select Course" button for that course should be disabled and a corresponding prompt should be displayed.
The graph structure on the course details page supports interactive operations (such as clicking on a node to view details, expanding/collapsing subtrees), and responds quickly.
checklist.bug: Non-foldable

checklist.content: The response time for all operations (course selection, course withdrawal, filtering, and searching) should be within a reasonable range, with no noticeable lag, and the page status should be updated in real time.

On the course details page, the system can dynamically display the complete prerequisite and dependent course links of the course in a graph structure. The graph structure is clear, readable, and the nodes are interactive.
The system can detect circular dependencies in prerequisite relations and highlight them in the graph structure or provide warnings.
The virtual timetable is displayed in a clear time grid or list format, clearly showing the class time, location, and duration of each course.
The system can accurately calculate the total credits for the user's current virtual timetable and clearly display them on the timetable interface.
The node states in the graph structure (such as selected, not selected, prerequisite satisfied/not satisfied) should have clear visual distinctions (such as different colors or icons).

checklist.content: Clicking/triggering view switching controls (such as buttons, drop-down menus, etc.)

Users can add steps one by one to describe the cooking process. Other users can browse all published recipes, view the full details of any recipe including all its steps, and leave comments on recipes they've tried. checklist.content: Users can create new recipes, including titles, descriptions, and ingredient lists.
Users can add one cooking step to a recipe at a time.
Users can publish completed recipes and make them visible to other users.
Users can browse a list of all published recipes.
Users can view complete details of the selected recipe, including the title, description, ingredients, and all cooking steps.
Users can leave comments on published recipes.
Users can rate recipes that they did not post themselves.
The rating record for a recipe will be saved after a user rates it.
